title: Keep initial native UI failure snapshots independent without renaming live driver paths

observedFailure.test: retained snapshots survive writes through an already-open driver log and include hidden debug evidence

scope.callerOwnership: The runner owns the spawnSync invocation and captures its stdout/stderr into settings-maestro.log after return; it does not own arbitrary surviving nested driver log handles.
scope.implementation: Leave failed settings and original command log at their existing paths, copy independent exclusive snapshots before recovery, and give only attempt 1 its own settings-retry directory/log/hierarchy/report paths.
unchanged: Exactly one authorized recovery; second failure final
Native binaries, workflows, deadlines and permissions
limits: V8 syntax/static and mocked-flow checks only; no actual Node filesystem or Windows/mobile execution of candidate
Existing actual open-descriptor append/rewrite/truncate regression is preserved for CI
Retained files are read-time snapshots before recovery, not atomic multi-file or complete post-exit logs
The separate release-readiness failure is not changed by this patch

edits.before:
logs: existing driver handles may still write to the original files, preserved
separately under `settings-initial-transport-live`. The scoped native evidence
uploads include the driver's hidden `debug/.maestro` logs. The installed app

edits.after:
logs: existing driver handles may still write to the original files, which stay
in `settings` with the original `settings-maestro.log` beside it. Keeping them in
place avoids renaming directories with open driver handles on Windows. The one
retry writes to `settings-retry` and its own command log and hierarchy; its flow
receipt names those actual paths. The scoped native evidence uploads include the
driver's hidden `debug/.maestro` logs. The installed app payload is unchanged.
The complete Settings flow then runs with the same semantic
